source.title: On the chain rule for the divergence of BV like vector fields: Applications, partial results, open problems

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be an open subset of R^d and let B be a locally BV, locally bounded vector field B in BV_loc(Omega; R^d) ∩ L^infty_loc(Omega; R^d). At points x where the distributional derivative DB has a finite polar blow-up limit M(x) = lim_{r downarrow 0} DB(B_r(x))/|DB|(B_r(x)) and B has a Lebesgue limit B_tilde(x), define the tangential set E of B by the condition M(x) · B_tilde(x) = 0. Must the Cantor part of the distributional divergence of B, denoted |D^c · B|, vanish on the tangential set E? This unrestricted assertion is false: there exists a BV vector field in R^2 for which |D^c · B|(E) is positive.

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be an open subset of R^d and let B be a locally BV, locally bounded vector field B in BV_loc(Omega; R^d) ∩ L^infty_loc(Omega; R^d). Using the tangential set E of B defined at points where DB has a finite polar blow-up limit M(x) and B has a Lebesgue limit B_tilde(x), with M(x) · B_tilde(x) = 0, what additional conditions on B ensure that the Cantor part of the distributional divergence, |D^c · B|, vanishes on E?

accepted.question_text: Let Omega be an open subset of R^d, let B be a locally BV, locally bounded vector field B in BV_loc(Omega; R^d) ∩ L^infty_loc(Omega; R^d), and let rho be a bounded scalar function on Omega such that rho is bounded below by a positive constant C and D · (rho B) = 0 in the sense of distributions. For this nearly-incompressible weighted divergence-free setting, is it true that the Cantor part of the distributional divergence of B, |D^c · B|, vanishes on the tangential set of B?

evidence.quote: Question 2. Let B∈B V loc ∩L∞ loc(Ω , R d) and let ρ∈L∞(Ω) be such that ρ≥C > 0 and D·(ρB) = 0. Is it true that |D c·B|vanishes on the tangential set of B?

accepted.question_text: Let b_n: R_t × R_x^d -> R^d be smooth vector fields and let Phi_n solve the ordinary differential equations d Phi_n(t,x)/dt = b_n(t, Phi_n(t,x)) with initial condition Phi_n(0,x) = x. Suppose the flows are nearly incompressible, meaning that there is a constant C such that C^{-1} <= det(nabla_x Phi_n(t,x)) <= C, and suppose the quantities ||b_n||_infty + ||nabla b_n||_{L^1} are uniformly bounded. Under these assumptions, must the sequence of flows {Phi_n} be strongly precompact in L^1_loc?
